- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.3), model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +0.8–1.2% bias to first 5 days to capture lagged momentum.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model overreacts to short-term noise; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
